newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: MALAYSIA PROPOSES A SINGLE TAX FOR TIMBER EXPORTS.
newsitem.headline: MALAYSIA PROPOSES A SINGLE TAX FOR TIMBER EXPORTS.

text.p: Malaysia is planning to introduce a single tax for timber exports to make its wood more competitive internationally, the national Bernama news agency reported on Thursday.
Three different sets of taxes now exist for timber in Malaysia, creating unhealthy competition, Bernama quoted Primary Industries Minister Lim Keng Yaik as saying.
Lim said the National Forestry Council, chaired by Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim, will decide on the proposal at a meeting early next year.
The bulk of Malaysia's timber is produced by Sabah and Sarawak, two states on Borneo island.
Both Sabah and Sarawak have their own timber laws and Lim has been trying for years to standardise the rules with those in force elsewhere in Malaysia.
Lim said it was important for Malaysia to have a uniform tax as the present levies were confusing.

He said Sarawak had the lowest levy and its sawn timber and plywood were among the cheapest -- so cheap they could be exported to Singapore and imported back into Malaysia's Johor state which borders Singapore.
Malaysia earned $5.5 billion, or about seven percent of its export earnings, through the sale of logs, sawn timber, plywood and other timber products last year.
